 Vehicle-seat architecture for time-dependent occupant trajectory management, controlled ride-down, progressive
 energy absorption, multi-state locking, and distributed load paths

 CRITICAL LEGAL / ENGINEERING STATUS
 Core disclosure thesis: the invention is not a literal local gravity generator. It is a seat system that time-programs the
 mechanical state of the seat and its force paths so that seat translation, rotation, restraint interaction, compliance
 and rebound are coordinated during a crash event. The effective-gravity interpretation is an inertial-frame concept,
 g_eff(t)=g-a_seat(t), not creation of a new gravitational field.

1. RUTHLESS PATENTABILITY ASSESSMENT
 The current concept contains valuable engineering structure, but several broad elements are already crowded by
 published vehicle-seat patents. A broad claim such as “seat + rail + energy absorber + inertial lock + seatback
 motion” would be vulnerable. The present draft therefore focuses on combinations and control relationships that are
 more specific: time-phased state transitions, decoupling of ride-down stroke from seatback rotation control,
 redundant parallel load paths, explicit rebound state, and coordinated occupant trajectory management.

 occupant-seat problem. The 2023 THOR-05F crash series used an instrumented advanced female ATD and

 NHTSA/SAE work compared THOR-50M, BioRID-II and PMHS responses and evaluated seatback rotation and occupant
 kinematics. The accompanying virtual-testing study used a validated Honda Accord seat FE model to study seat
 collapse and strengthening under scaled rear-impact pulses.

 specific hardware (cam/pawl, hydraulic cartridge, crush element, sensor/actuator type) into dependent claims unless

  V7-6. THOR-05F / NHTSA Methodology - Correct Scope
  The 2023 THOR-05F material is used as a methodology benchmark for rigorous occupant-safety experimentation: defined
  seating posture, instrumentation, calibration/qualification, repeated checks and post-test inspection. It is not claimed as the
  T-OCS mechanism.

  The 2025 rear-impact work compares THOR-50M, BioRID-II and PMHS and explicitly notes limitations from sample size and
  differences between sled and full-vehicle conditions. This supports a staged validation plan rather than a single simulation claim.
  ■filecite■turn5file4■L499-L503■
  The PMHS material also shows that injury-related seat design cannot be reduced to one scalar force: the reported summary links
  fracture distribution to seatback properties and describes combined thoracic loading and pelvic off-axis rotation.
  ■filecite■turn5file3■L458-L458■

  written-description support, and finalize claim language and drawings.

  6. Detailed Mechanism Disclosure
  A. Dual-rail ride-down carriage: the seat carriage translates relative to the vehicle structure through a guided path. Each side
  carries a defined portion of the reaction load and can include an absorber or a redundant structural path.

  B. Independent seatback rotation control: the seatback frame is constrained by a separate bilateral path that can include
  links, dampers, torsional elements or hard stops. This path is intentionally not identical to the energy-stroke path.

  C. Multi-state lock: the lock mechanism is disclosed generically to permit cam/pawl, wedge, dog-clutch, pin, ratchet or
  equivalent constructions. The inventive point is its state coordination with ride-down and rebound, not the existence of an
  inertial pawl itself.

  D. Energy absorber: the replaceable cartridge is characterized by F(x), F(t), hysteresis and temperature response. The design
  package uses the nominal 180 mm concept stroke, but this remains a design assumption until derived from a vehicle-specific
  crash

  discipline

  12. Safety / Fail-Safe Disclosure
  The primary occupant restraint path remains available even if the optional ride-down trigger does not arm. The system should
  default to a mechanically safe state when trigger, sensor, actuator, or power availability is lost.

  Required design reviews before any human-subject or vehicle-crash use:
  • Single-point failure and common-cause failure analysis for the lock/trigger.

  • Mechanical stop analysis at both stroke ends.

  • Over-travel and jam analysis for both rails.

  • Asymmetric-load analysis for one-sided absorber or link degradation.

  • Temperature and contamination sensitivity of seals, springs, damping fluid and locks.

  • Belt/airbag interaction and anchorage load validation.

  • Post-crash inspection/replacement rules for serviceable absorber cartridges.

  V7-6. THOR-05F / NHTSA Methodology - Correct Scope
  The 2023 THOR-05F material is used as a methodology benchmark for rigorous occupant-safety experimentation: defined
  seating posture, instrumentation, calibration/qualification, repeated checks and post-test inspection. It is not claimed as the
  T-OCS mechanism.

  The 2025 rear-impact work compares THOR-50M, BioRID-II and PMHS and explicitly notes limitations from sample size and
  differences between sled and full-vehicle conditions. This supports a staged validation plan rather than a single simulation claim.
  ■filecite■turn5file4■L499-L503■
  The PMHS material also shows that injury-related seat design cannot be reduced to one scalar force: the reported summary links
  fracture distribution to seatback properties and describes combined thoracic loading and pelvic off-axis rotation.
  ■filecite■turn5file3■L458-L458■

  9. Source-Derived Engineering Basis
  The supplied THOR-05F material provides a model for professional validation discipline rather than a technology source for the
  invention. It shows that advanced occupant testing requires extensive instrumentation, defined seating posture,
  calibration/qualification, repeated checks and post-test inspection. ■filecite■turn2file4■L286-L299■

  The supplied PMHS rear-facing frontal study is particularly useful because it shows why a single scalar force target is
  inadequate: rib fracture distribution depended on seatback properties and combined thoracic loading, while pelvic outward
  deformation was associated with off-axis rotations. ■filecite■turn5file3■L458-L458■

  The 2025 NHTSA/SAE biofidelity work also emphasizes the distinction between sled and full-vehicle conditions and the limited
  injury conclusions possible from a small sample. ■filecite■turn5file4■L499-L503■

  The FMVSS 214 laboratory procedure in the supplied document is treated as a methodological reference for side-impact test
  discipline
